entry.summary:

The Price of Greed

🔹A fox happened to fall into a well bucket and, as the rope turned, went down to the bottom of the well. Struggle as it might, it found no way out—until a hungry wolf came to the well's edge and lowered its head.

🔹The clever fox put on an act and cried out: "Down here a feast of food and comfort awaits, but I can't manage it alone; if you'd like to share the meal, get into the upper bucket so you can come down to me!"

🔹The greedy wolf leapt without a moment's hesitation and sat in the upper bucket. Since the wolf was heavier, its bucket hurtled downward, and at the same time the rope turned and drew the fox's bucket upward.

🔹Midway up the well, the two buckets passed each other. The wolf cried out in astonishment: "Where are you off to, friend?!"

🔹The fox laughed and said: "That's the way of this wheel of fortune—unless one goes down, the other never comes up!" The fox reached the bright mouth of the well and sprang out, while the wolf was left behind in the dark depths.

#حکایت@Farsna

While Iran Khodro speaks of 78% localization and Saipa of 81% localization, and the assemblers also have a share of less than 40%, the question arises as to why localization has not been able to protect prices against currency shocks.
🔸To curb this cycle and cut the car market's psychological and real dependence on the dollar, the policymaker has no choice but to open the doors to targeted imports at times when relative stability prevails in the management of the country's foreign exchange resources, so that part of the foreign currency is allocated to the entry of economy cars—a strategy that can break the monopoly and save the market from profiteering./ Fars

entry.summary:

Source: @FarsNA

Domestic car prices are peaking ahead of the dollar🔹Car prices in the market have become sticky to the currency—a trend that accelerates upward whenever the exchange rate climbs. Today, cars that were once considered economy models have crossed into the billions of tomans.🔹This dependence on the currency, especially over the past year, has opened a deep gap between people's purchasing power and real prices. Last autumn, around this same time, the market was at completely different price levels, but persistent currency instability released the spring of prices.🔹Market statistics from the past year lay bare the depth of this jump: the Dena Automatic, which was around 1 billion and 300 million tomans at this point last year, has now reached about 4 billion tomans, and in the assembled-products segment, Lamari has climbed from 2 billion and 500 million tomans last year to 7 billion and 400 million tomans.🔹The car market's dependence on dollar fluctuations stands in clear contradiction to the claim of self-sufficiency. While Iran Khodro cites 78 percent localization and Saipa 81 percent, and assemblers hold a share of less than 40 percent, the question arises: why has localization failed to shield prices from currency shocks?🔸To curb this cycle and sever the car market's psychological and real dependence on the dollar, policymakers have no choice but to open the doors to targeted imports at times when relative stability prevails in the country's management of currency resources, so that part of the currency is channeled into bringing in economy cars—a strategy that can break the monopoly and rescue the market from profiteering.@Farsna - Link

One of the important yet under-examined questions in Iran's contemporary history is why Iran, in the age of colonialism, despite its economic and military weakness and its proximity to two great imperial powers, managed to preserve its political independence and avoid becoming a formal colony. In the nineteenth century, before the discovery of oil, Iran—unlike India—did not possess vast, contiguous agricultural lands with a high capacity for producing commercial crops. Unlike China, it had no consumer market with a population in the hundreds of millions, and unlike certain other territories, known gold and silver mines were not the primary source of its economic appeal to colonial powers. Nor was Iran part of the Ottoman Empire, such that it would have been caught up in the partition of Ottoman territories among the European powers. Nevertheless, Iran held extraordinary geopolitical importance. Its geographic position—between Tsarist Russia and British-ruled India—had made the country one of the most important arenas of imperial rivalry. Under such circumstances, Iran's survival cannot be attributed merely to chance or to a lack of resources attractive to colonialists. entry.title: [FarsNA] New details on the wells that swallowed Parishan's share🔹The global…
entry.summary:
Machine-translated from the original Telegram post.

Source: @FarsNA

New details on the wells that swallowed Parishan's share🔹The global registration of Gahar Lake in Lorestan under the Ramsar Convention has once again drawn attention to the status of Iran's registered wetlands.🔹Some of these wetlands have been grappling with drought for years and are still deprived of their water rights and an effective plan to restore natural conditions.🔹Parishan Wetland in Fars Province, with nearly two decades of poor conditions and hundreds of water-extraction wells, and Gavkhouni Wetland in Isfahan Province, despite the allocation of water rights and water releases into the Zayandeh Rud, are two examples of this situation.🔹Parishan Wetland has been in poor condition for about 16 to 18 years. One of the main reasons for this is the wetland's particular hydrological characteristics.🔹Parishan is one of the few wetlands in the country that does not lie at the end of a permanent river's course and has no direct river inflow. Its main source of water is rainfall and the floods that occur in the region.🔹For this reason, Parishan is more fragile than wetlands fed by permanent rivers.🔹When the groundwater table was high, rainfall would saturate the soil and raise the wetland's water level.🔹In fact, the connection between rainfall, the aquifer, and the wetland was such that water could quickly accumulate in the region and create suitable conditions for the wetland.🔹But in recent years, with increased extraction from groundwater resources, this situation has changed. There are about 490 illegal wells in the Parishan area.🖼But what plan is in place to prevent these conditions from continuing?Read here@Farsna

In these questions, the Alberta government is not merely seeking to change executive policies but is calling for a constitutional amendment and a redefinition of the legal relationship between the federal government and the provinces. From February 28 to today, gasoline has gotten more expensive in 145 countries. 29 countries have seen serious street protests. Paris made 1,800 arrests in a single day, Bolivia saw 17 killed, and in Tirana government buildings went up in flames.

So the short answer is: yes, the shock of this war reached the entire world.

But the chart says something else too — something more important.

Point one: Nigeria had a 75 percent fuel price hike and stayed calm. Albania had 17 percent and went up in flames.

▪️Stating that unless it is determined how much responsibility each party bears for derailing the agreement, and as long as leniency is shown in this regard, support campaigns will not achieve the desired outcome, he said: Supporting the agreement requires, beyond civil actions and popular campaigns, serious and responsible action by official authorities, especially the government.

▪️Ali Mehrabadi noted that despite the follow-ups, no permit has yet been issued for a gathering in support of the agreement, which the Reform Front of Iran had previously requested, and added: As long as marginal confrontations and the chanting of harsh slogans continue at nighttime gatherings, and no appropriate action is taken by official authorities — particularly the government — to manage these conditions, such campaigns in support of the agreement will yield little and will not be widely embraced by the public.

▪️In conclusion, the Head of the Reform Front of Hamadan Province, while commending the intentions of the organizers of these campaigns, expressed hope that these efforts will bear fruit, and emphasized: Alongside these actions, it is essential that Mr. Pezeshkian and the government take serious and effective measures to support those who find themselves in these difficult conditions.

🔹The Reform Front of Iran's address on social networks: Telegram, Instagram, X (Twitter)

Amir Mohammad Hatami, an 18-year-old from Shahin Shahr in Isfahan, was killed by a point-blank shot to his right eye after being wounded and taken into custody on the evening of 19 Dey. After 20 days of searching prisons, morgues, and security centers, his family finally identified his body—which bore signs of torture—by an old scar on his right shoulder. The 18-year-old was of Bakhtiari origin and lived in Shahin Shahr in Isfahan province. In the first days, Hatami's family had no information about their son's detention and did not know where he had been taken after being wounded. According to a source close to the family, during the search, Hatami's family would open about 100 black body bags every day in the hope of finding their son. Finally, after 20 days of searching, someone contacted the family and asked them to send a family member to identify a body. The source said: "When we went to identify Amir Mohammad, his body was inside a black bag. The blood on his body had dried and he was unrecognizable. His body and face were completely bruised." He added that Amir Mohammad's ears were severely damaged, his eyes had been gouged out, and numerous marks of injury were visible on his body. Amir Mohammad worked as a mechanic. According to those close to him, despite his young age, he was highly skilled in this trade and was known as "Osta" in Shahin Shahr. Those who knew Amir Mohammad described him as a hardworking, kind, and responsible young man who, in addition to helping provide for his family, also cared about supporting child laborers. iranintl 📡 @VahidOnline

But only to create instability.

I've been holding on to this video for several years now, to attach to a note in my journals about left and right (which I still haven't had the chance to finish).

Although the concepts of left and right are inadequate and vague for capturing the complexities of today's global political landscape, they can still be somewhat useful for conveying and understanding messages.

In this video, Bezmenov, a KGB associate and insider, explains that using leftists is useful—"but only up to the point of creating instability in countries."

The interview was recorded in 1984.

Link

Let me emphasize once again: if you ask my opinion, for our country today we want neither left nor right. What we want is a different way of looking at things—one that aligns with the left on some positions and with the right on others.

Almost the opposite of most of those segments that have today been adopted from—or have ended up aligning with—the conventional left and right in our political structure.

entry.title: [mostafamalekian] 🔴Not every belief that keeps us alive is necessarily true. "Practical…
entry.summary:
Machine-translated from the original Telegram post.

Source: @mostafamalekian

🔴Not every belief that keeps us alive is necessarily true. "Practical usefulness does not imply theoretical truth." ✍ Mostafa Malekian

🔹The fact that a belief helps us in practice, solves a problem, or even contributes to our survival does not by itself show that the belief corresponds to reality. Being useful is one thing; being true is another. You cannot infer the latter from the former.

A medicine may cure our headache, yet the theory on which the medicine was based may not be correct. The drug's effectiveness in curing does not by itself prove the correctness of the theory behind it.

The same distinction must be kept in mind in the discussion of evolution. If we accept Darwin's theory, we must note that the persistence of our beliefs, feelings, emotions, and desires does not necessarily mean they show us the truth; they may have persisted because they helped preserve the survival of our species.

That something ensures the survival of the human species is different from its expressing the truth. We may have held a belief, and that very belief kept our species alive; but from this one cannot conclude that the belief was certainly correct. It is even possible that awareness of a truth, rather than aiding our survival, endangers it.

🔹When people have said since ancient times that "the truth is bitter," one of its meanings is this: what is true is not always life-preserving for us or a guarantor of our continued existence.

🔹Therefore, even if a belief seems perfectly clear and self-evident to us and generation after generation has lived with it, this mere persistence and usefulness does not prove that it is true.

🔹From the fact that "this belief has helped our survival," one cannot conclude that "therefore this belief is true."

➖Part of the lecture "Critique_of_the_Book_Analytical_Idealism" @mostafamalekian

"Feeling the Sorrow of Others" in a Tale by Saadi

You've heard me say this a lot, but since I…
entry.summary:
Machine-translated from the original Telegram post.

Source: @bamotamem

Strategy at the Individual Level

You've heard me say this a lot, but since I brought up resource constraints, I'd like to repeat it once more:

Whenever someone tells me, "Starting today, I want to do such-and-such" (study a language, read books, exercise, ...),

my first question to them is:

"What are you going to stop doing starting today?" Because your day wasn't 23.5 hours before, that you'd now want to add half an hour to it. Until yesterday you also had 24 hours, and now you want to add a quarter hour or half an hour of a new activity to it. So something has to give.

Now either you're going to watch fewer movies,
or go to fewer parties,
or sleep less,
or exercise less,
or check Instagram and Telegram less,
or ...

If someone hasn't clearly answered this second question, that first thing they said is just a passing fad. Sooner or later, you should expect them to rattle off all sorts of excuses for "it not working out" and "giving up."

Being Iranian is a blend of wisdom, justice, liberty, and love—four pillars on which our culture rests. A culture's pillars should not be judged merely by how faithfully people adhere to them today; we must also ask what values a culture possesses that enable it to recognize and correct its own shortcomings. These four pillars are not a claim that Iranians are flawless; they are an ethical and cultural horizon we can lean on to build a better society. Wisdom, justice, liberty, and love are neither imported values nor newly invented ideals; they are rooted in our own history and intellectual and cultural heritage. From the Avesta and the teachings of truth and asha, to the admonition books of ancient Iran and their emphasis on wisdom and justice; from Ferdowsi's Shahnameh and its praise of wisdom, justice, and liberty, to the works of Saadi and other great figures of Persian literature who have honored love and humanism—the continuity of these values is visible. These four pillars are not meant to describe the behavior of all Iranians in all eras. They are criteria rooted in our culture, and we can even draw on them to critique the shortcomings of today's society. If there is foolishness, wisdom remains a virtue; if there is injustice, justice remains a value; if there is baseness and flattery, liberty remains an ideal; and if there is violence and hatred, love remains an ethical necessity.

entry.title:
[bamotamem] Strategy hurts (1)
Following my previous point about the vision, it's worth…
entry.summary:
Machine-translated from the original Telegram post.

Source: @bamotamem

Strategy hurts (1)

Following my previous point about the vision, it's worth adding a few more notes. I've said these things many times over the years. But repeating them is useful too. They're worth constantly repeating and hearing.

My friends.

Strategy is always and always accompanied by resource allocation. The resources at our disposal (money, time, connections, etc.) are limited, and strategy is supposed to help us allocate these limited resources better.

"Resource allocation" is different from "resource distribution."

Resource distribution means I spread whatever I have across different tasks, different resources, different departments, and try to make sure everyone gets a piece.

Resource allocation is a scientific and precise term with a specific meaning.

Resource allocation means we think about who we want to give these limited resources to (and who we don't).

By defining, formulating, and executing strategy, we always create dissatisfied people. If you see that a strategy meeting was held, everyone sat together and talked, and at the end everyone came out smiling, know that the only thing wasted in there was the sugar and tea and the fruit of the meeting.

Must, must, must, some people come out of the strategy meeting upset. These are the same managers, the same departments, and the same projects that have been allocated fewer resources.

#استراتژی

"Feeling the Sorrow of Others" in a Tale by Saadi

In his tale of the Damascus famine, Saadi speaks of a man who is not himself in straitened circumstances, yet the suffering of the hungry robs him of pleasure. Can one, in a time of war, economic hardship, and insecurity, be concerned about the suffering of others and still carry on with life?

In this episode, inspired by Saadi's tale, we turn to the meaning of empathy in difficult days; we speak about the necessity of compassion and of lessening the suffering of others, and we reflect on how the flood of images of suffering on social media can gradually numb us. entry.title: [mostafamalekian] 🔴Can one be a materialist without denying God? | The difference between…
entry.summary:
Machine-translated from the original Telegram post.

Source: @mostafamalekian

🔴Can one be a materialist without denying God? | The difference between materialism and moral materialism ✍ Mostafa Malekian

Materialism comes in two very distinct forms: one is "philosophical materialism" and the other is "moral materialism" or "value materialism." To clarify the difference, we need to see what each one claims.

Who is a materialist in the philosophical sense?

Philosophical materialism is a view of the universe. Those who hold this view believe that nothing exists in the world unless it is the product of the exchange of matter and energy—that is, the product of matter converting into energy or energy converting into matter.

🔹But what about our mind and our mental states? Materialists hold two positions here: Some say that mind and mental states do not exist at all. If we ask why we believe they exist, they answer that this belief is a product of our "folk psychology"; it is within this psychology that something called mind and mental states appears to exist.

🔹Others say that mind and mental states do exist, but they are reducible to the same exchange of matter and energy. In a sense, mind and mental phenomena too seem to be wearing a disguise; otherwise, they too are simply material phenomena.

🔹With such a view, one can no longer believe in the existence of God or a non-material spirit and soul. This is philosophical materialism—a view that many philosophers have held throughout history.

But what is moral materialism?

Moral materialism has nothing to do with philosophical materialism at all; rather, it is a theory in axiology whose gist is this: the only thing that matters in life is wealth.

Here I use "wealth" in a sense that also includes money, property, and assets.

If you believe that in human life only one thing has value, and that is wealth, you are a moral materialist. Since value means having importance, it can be put more simply: in this view, only wealth is important and nothing else in life matters.

According to this view, wealth—for having a good and ideal life—is both a "necessary condition" and a "sufficient condition":

• Necessary condition means that unless you are wealthy, you will not have a good life.

• Sufficient condition means that if you have wealth, you no longer need anything else for a good life.

Most of us human beings, in most historical periods, have not been materialists in the first sense; but the majority of us are materialists in the second sense.

➖From the lecture "Balance and Equilibrium between Money and Spirituality"
@mostafamalekian
